title: Continuous functions on limits of F-decomposable systems: an LUR renorming of $C(X)$ for $F_d$-compacta (main theorem)
author: Todor Manev
work: Continuous functions on limits of F-decomposable systems
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's main theorem (source0.tex lines 382-384), that the space of continuous functions on an F_d-compact of countable spectral height admits an equivalent LUR norm that is lower semicontinuous for the pointwise topology. The retained complete proof (lines 386-457) is a genuine 72-line argument, not a routine verification: it constructs a countable family of continuous functions and open covers refining the F-decomposable inverse system, uses the metrizability criterion for fully closed mappings and the finite-branching lemma to control the fibres, transfers the countable decomposition characterization of Molto-Orihuela-Troyanski from a norming subspace to the pointwise topology, and then assembles the local uniformly rotund norm from the resulting decomposition while keeping the sigma(E,F)-lower semicontinuity. The residual difficulty is that a topological decomposition of a non-metrizable compactum must be converted into a renorming whose unit sphere is pointwise closed; this is research-level Banach space topology well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
